test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 09 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements best defines the monoecious?

options.text: A flower with both androecium and gynoecium

solution:
The correct answer is __**A flower with both androecium and gynoecium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Monoecious plants** have both male (androecium) and female (gynoecium) reproductive organs in the same plant.
 
• This characteristic allows monoecious plants to self-pollinate, although cross-pollination can also occur.
 
• Examples of monoecious plants include maize, cucumbers, and squash.
 
• Monoecious plants are different from dioecious plants, which have male and female reproductive organs on separate plants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Androecium**

 
 
• The androecium is the male reproductive part of a flower.
 
• It consists of stamens, each of which has a filament topped by an anther where pollen is produced.
 
 
 
• **Gynoecium**
 
 
• The gynoecium is the female reproductive part of a flower.
 
• It consists of one or more carpels, each containing an ovary, style, and stigma.
 
• The ovary contains ovules, which develop into seeds upon fertilization.
 
 
 
• **Dioecious**
 
 
• Dioecious plants have male and female reproductive organs on separate plants.
 
• This means that a dioecious plant is either male or female, not both.
 
• Examples of dioecious plants include holly, willow, and asparagus.
 
 
 
• **Pollination**
 
 
• Pollination is the process by which pollen is transferred from the male part of a plant to the female part, allowing fertilization to occur.
 
• Pollination can be carried out by wind, water, insects, birds, and other animals.
 
• Self-pollination occurs within the same flower or plant, while cross-pollination occurs between different plants.
